---
title: "The engine"
subtitle: "Run Raccoon locally, or embed it in your own tool"
---

The engine that plays you in the browser is the same one you can download and
run yourself. It is MIT-licensed and written in Python and PyTorch, with game
rules from [OpenSpiel](https://openspiel.readthedocs.io/).

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/lassehjorthmadsen/raccoon.git
cd raccoon
make setup          # editable install with dev dependencies
make test           # run the test suite
make play           # play against Raccoon in the terminal
```

## What the network is

| | |
|---|---|
| Architecture | 10-block, 256-channel residual network — {{< var engine.params >}} parameters |
| Input | A (26, 2, 12) tensor: checker planes, bar/borne-off/dice broadcasts, and handcrafted pip, blot, anchor and contact features |
| Value head | Six mutually exclusive outcomes — win, gammon, backgammon, each way — from which cubeless equity follows |
| Move selection | 0-ply value lookahead: every legal play is evaluated in one batched forward pass, no search |
| Training | Supervised distillation of 40M positions labelled by GNU Backgammon's 2-ply search |

## Strength

Scored on the [BGSage money benchmark](https://research.raccoonbg.com) —
{{< var engine.pr_n >}} checker decisions with rollout-quality cubeless-equity
references. PR is mean move-selection error × 500; lower is better.

| Engine | Compute per decision | PR |
|---|---|---|
| GNU Backgammon, 2-ply full-width search | ~1.3 s | **{{< var engine.gnubg_2ply_pr >}}** |
| **Raccoon `{{< var engine.network >}}`, single evaluation** | ~10 ms | **{{< var engine.pr >}}** |
| GNU Backgammon, single evaluation (0-ply) | ~10 ms | **{{< var engine.gnubg_0ply_pr >}}** |

In head-to-head play against GNU Backgammon at 0-ply, Raccoon wins
**{{< var engine.ppg_edge >}} points per game** over {{< var engine.ppg_n >}}
cubeless money games scored with variance-reduced rollouts.

Two thirds of that margin came from fixing the *search*, not the network: on a
double the engine used to pick its four half-moves two at a time instead of
optimising the whole turn, which cost 0.033 points per game. The browser engine
optimises doubles jointly, like the measured one.

The browser runs this network exported to ONNX. That exported file was scored on
the same benchmark, at the same sample size, and lands on the same number
(PR 0.9500 for the ONNX file versus 0.9498 for the PyTorch checkpoint,
n = {{< var engine.pr_n >}}) — so the engine you play here is the engine that was
measured, not a reduced version of it.

**What it does not do yet:** the doubling cube. Play here and in the CLI is
cubeless money game. Cube handling is the next milestone.

## Embedding it

The engine speaks the Raccoon Game Protocol, a UCI-style line protocol over
stdin/stdout intended for analysis GUIs. See
[`raccoon/protocol/rgp.py`](https://github.com/lassehjorthmadsen/raccoon/blob/main/raccoon/protocol/rgp.py)
and the [architecture notes](https://research.raccoonbg.com/architecture.html).
If you are building a tool and want to embed Raccoon,
[get in touch](contact.qmd).
